reason: The premise is factually false and the fix, driven, is worse. (1) The slabs are not "the only filled rectangles in a system otherwise built entirely from hairlines": b.css draws the row plate filled at --fore-04 with border-radius 4px on hover (l.366), at --fore-06 with 4px while editing (l.373-374), at --back with 4px when crowded (l.371), and every press state in the product - .b-item:active .b-copy, .b-grab:active, .b-act:active, .b-step:active, .b-behindSummary:active, .b-undoAct:active (l.688-693) - is background: var(--fore-10). The skeleton is background: var(--fore-10); border-radius: 4px (l.1184): the exact tint and the exact radius the product already uses for a pressed surface, and 4 is on the declared radii ladder (0,4,6,8,12,16,24,999). The docked editor is a filled --fore-06 panel (l.712-713), primary actions are solid --fore plates (l.649), the pressed segment is a solid plate (l.805), the unfurl card is a solid --ink plate (l.1038). "Nothing in the finished plan is a rounded grey block" is contradicted by the state the owner is in whenever they edit a row. The reserve is drawn in the system's lowest rung of ink density, which is exactly the constraint's stated mechanism ("hierarchy is expressed by ink density"). (2) The fix invents a token. There is no --fore-12: shell.css l.161-182 declares 90/72/62/46/28/16/10/06/04 only. I applied the fix verbatim in Chromium at 390x844 and border-bottom-color computed to rgb(255,255,255) - the undefined var falls back to currentColor, so the "hairlines" render at FULL white, brighter than any rule in the product and brighter than the today rule sitting 26px below them. Adding a --fore-12 would put a new alpha on a ladder that has none. (3) Rendered with the nearest real token (--fore-16) it is plainly worse: the numeral's 107x86 outlined empty square with square corners reads as a broken-image glyph, and the three remaining under-rules land at the same 1px --fore-16 weight as the real divider beneath them, so the frame becomes a blank form with fill-in underlines and the audience can no longer tell reserve from structure. A 1px rule at the foot of 86px of nothing also stops saying that a 96px figure is coming - it keeps the layout reserve while destroying the visual one, which is the half of "the loading frame says what is coming" the gate cannot measure. The seat's own paragraph concedes the reserve is honest and correctly sized; what is left is a restyle onto a vocabulary the product does not have, away from one it demonstrably does.
